title: CoT-Faithfulness Hint-Acknowledgment Replicated on Control Tasks

original_idea.body:
# CoT-Faithfulness Hint-Acknowledgment Replicated on Control Tasks

**Problem:** Faithfulness studies show models often use injected hints/cues without verbalizing them in their CoT; this unfaithfulness has mostly been studied on QA, not on control-relevant deceptive tasks.

**Direction:** Replicate the hint-injection faithfulness test on a control setting: inject a subtle cue that nudges an open model toward inserting a backdoor or pursuing a side goal, and measure how often the model acts on the cue without mentioning it in its CoT. Twist: relate CoT-mention rate to whether a CoT monitor catches the resulting attack.

**Why it matters:** CoT monitoring assumes the CoT reveals the real reason for an action. Showing models act on hidden cues silently in a control context directly bounds CoT-monitor reliability and is fully reproducible with open weights.

**Relevant context:** CoT faithfulness literature on unverbalized hint use; 'Can Reasoning Models Obfuscate Reasoning?' (arXiv 2510.19851) shows benign external CoT with identical malicious tool calls. APPS backdoor setting for the action.
